panels.title: Shared VM runner pool · WK01 + master

options.content:
Stable slots per host · 30-second sampling · shared across both organisations. **Reserved VM slots includes warm spares and every VM lifecycle state. Warm VMs are already included in that total. Unallocated slots are capacity to prepare VMs, not ready runners.** Use Slot state history to distinguish Preparing, Ready spare and Runner launched; launched does not prove a job is busy.

Usage gaps mean stale, invalid or missing observations. Pool history starts at the first scrape; existing host history is unchanged. VM time is a sampled lifecycle estimate and gaps can undercount.

**Job success/failure is not collected.** Quarantine does not identify a failed job. Sampled time is not exact job duration or billable time.

Queued admitted jobs is the latest GitHub queue snapshot and can include jobs whose VM is already reserved or preparing. Queue and VM observations refresh independently. Unadmitted recipes and workflow concurrency-held jobs are excluded; queue observations older than 300 seconds are Unknown. WK01 gets first choice; master handles overflow, while its blank warm spares may exist before WK01 is full. Cold VM preparation is serial per host.

Both hosts are shown by default. Fleet counts require fresh, valid observations from WK01 and master: initial verified capacity is 10 + 2; 18 appears only after master admission and observations verify eight active slots. Missing or stale hosts leave fleet totals unknown. Master slots 0–3 belong to NUMA node 0 and slots 4–7 to node 1; initial slots are 0 and 4. Queue demand is observed once on WK01. History starts at the first scrape, without backfill. CPU ceilings are observed per host, not a shared fleet policy measurement.
